source.scope: 22 museum-backed taxon concepts; not direct live botanical measurements

comparative_design.stage_A: First verify original authority states on living head-stage matched same-population plants; stage and taxon identity before observation; phenological stage cannot be held at a single state across bud and fruit without repeated recording.
comparative_design.stage_B: Compare three nodding morph configurations on their actual gap geometry, direct actual spine length/rigidity, sticky exudates, rain wetting, and natural guild-specific approach/entry under equal hours and blinded labels, retaining species/site as nonexchangeable strata.
comparative_design.stage_C: Test whether coarse nodding orientation predicts similar routes but posture yields different entry probability; explicitly measure seed-feeder eggs, early parasitoid probing and filled viable seeds; no inference from mere posture co-occurrence.

contrasting_falsifiable_mechanisms.prediction: In similarly nodding heads, spread posture has wider validated real access gaps and greater successful external enemy access than appressed posture conditional on approach.
contrasting_falsifiable_mechanisms.rival: Posture label does not correspond to real gaps, spines fully dominate, phenophase or head diameter accounts for the difference.

contrasting_falsifiable_mechanisms.prediction: All nodding heads share lower pollen wetting during matched rain events regardless of phyllary posture; no necessary antipredator route change.
contrasting_falsifiable_mechanisms.rival: Actual aperture orientation and bract wetting control pollen viability rather than coarse O.

contrasting_falsifiable_mechanisms.prediction: Different phyllary postures partition legitimate pollen contact vs external oviposition and early parasitoid access in distinct ratios.
contrasting_falsifiable_mechanisms.rival: All guilds reach the disc from the same head-centred approach; posture gives neither selectivity nor fitness difference.

contrasting_falsifiable_mechanisms.prediction: State differences alone do not establish correlational selection, evolved compensation or historical same-branch transitions.
contrasting_falsifiable_mechanisms.rival: Independent population/genomic transitions plus selection needed.
